Safe Haven

By: Susan Comrie | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A place of safety that is anything but for young victims of abuse.

Summary:
This is a story about Jedidiah Safe Haven in Haarties run by Stephanie Bentley. In 2012 three young children burned to death in a fire on the property. By all accounts this was a tragic accident, but since then another child has died, two have been removed by the court, volunteers have come forward with evidence and allegations of verbal and physical abuse, and the organization’s own auditor has raised red flags about their accounting practices. Belatedly, the Department of Social Development has decided to deregister the home and has instructed Christelike Maatskaplike Raad (CMR) to remove all of their children from Jedidiah. But almost two months later, ten children are still in Stephanie’s care. We ask, with clear evidence of abuse, why have the police not acted, and why were CMR children removed while the State’s wards have remained in this unhealthy environment?

Further information:
Jedidiah Safe Haven has been in operation since 2008. It is a shelter run by Stephanie Bentley on the property owned by her husband, Rob. Safe Haven is supposed to provide temporary safe care for children who have been removed from their parents by the State. But it also makes private arrangements with parents to take on troubled teens, and when funds are running low homeless families or single mothers are invited to live on the property in exchange for cleaning and child care services. And although this is supposed to be a temporary home, many children have languished here for years.
In 2012 three children died when the wendy-house they were sleeping in burnt down. By all accounts this was a tragic accident – the result of children playing with or having matches and candles in a wooden wendy-house. The deaths were widely publicized and reported on, but it appears that there was no proper investigation into the deaths and the question of whether Stephanie and her staff had been negligent. Should the deaths have raised red flags? Should it have triggered even a routine investigation by the police or the Department of Social Development?
Had such an investigation been done they may have found evidence of the following:
• Mental and verbal abuse
• Physical abuse
• Statutory rape
Last year a police reservist approached Carte Blanche with allegations of these issues. He in turn put us in touch with a former volunteer as well as a former resident who also claimed to know about abuse at the home. The former resident – Charmaine – handed over audio and video recordings of going-on at Safe Haven. She claims to have recorded these on her cellphone in the weeks prior to her being evicted from the home.
The recordings suggest the children are mentally and verbally abused by Stephanie. There are also suggestions of physical and sexual abuse, but these are not explicit.
This evidence was handed over to the Department of Social Development last year who instructed CMR to remove their kids from Safe Haven. But three months later the State's own wards have remained in this unhealthy environment, including a 15-year-old girl who according to sources is pregnant with Stephanie's son's child and recently married him despite being under the age of consent. We have also spoken to Safe Haven's former auditor who has confirmed that there are many questionable practices with their finances which led him to issue them with a qualified audit.
We intend to approach the Department of Social Development to ask them to work with us to remove the remaining children from Safe Haven. Although the Department is unlikely to come off looking good, the blame appears to lie with the provincial Department, and action by the Minister may put her in a good light. We intend to conduct interviews with the various sources before the Department removes the kids so that we will be ready to confront Stephanie and run the story as soon as the kids are removed.

Press Release:


It’s meant to be a safe home for abused and neglected children. Instead, there’s verbal and physical abuse, underage sex and teen pregnancy. Carte Blanche investigates a ‘safe haven’ that seems anything but.

Script:


Not for children or sensitive viewers.

Derek Watts (Carte Blanche presenter): “Behind me is the idyllic valley of Hartbeespoort. But it’s in this quiet neighbourhood that we found a group of children living in a ‘safe haven’ that is anything but peaceful or safe...”

Stephanie Bentley: “This is a p**slike, f**king pig whorehouse here.”

The voice you’re hearing belongs to this woman – Stephanie Bentley [on screen]. And the place she’s talking about is Jedidiah Safe Haven, a home she runs for abused children.

Stephanie: “If I was a donor, and would give this f**ked up, dirty, p**s, c**p place money…”

Every year, thousands of South African children are abandoned, orphaned or removed from their families. For the past five years, Stephanie has been fostering some of these neglected kids at a property her husband owns in Hartbeespoort in the North West Province. There are sometimes as many as 50 children in her care, many placed by the State.

Charmaine Moodley (Former employee): “At first it was very nice. After a while then I started seeing things are not so okay there.”

This is Charmaine Moodley [on screen]. She and her two children worked at Jedidiah Safe Haven for several months last year – in exchange for board and lodging.

Charmaine: “She used to scream at the children, and you know, swear and things like that.”

Stephanie: “Close the f**king door so that the kids can’t go in there!”

Jedidiah Safe Haven wasn’t on anyone’s radar before a tragic accident in 2012 claimed the lives of Norman Khoza, his brother Laurence, and their cousin Given Matlala. A case was opened, but two years later, police say they’re still investigating. At the time, the Hartbeespoort community rallied round with donations. But six months ago, Carte Blanche first heard rumours of wide-ranging abuse at the home. We began speaking to concerned onlookers about Stephanie’s behaviour.

Charmaine: “When she’s cross with the children, when the children don’t listen to her, then she’ll hit them, you know... smack them through the face or something.”

Like Charmaine, Maryna Botes also helped at Jedidiah in exchange for a place to stay. She told us about the alleged abuse of a young girl in Stephanie’s care.

Maryna Botes (Former employee): “(Name withheld) place was not right, her clothes were on the floor. I stood next to Tannie Steph; she couldn’t find anything to hit the child with, but one of those small cricket bats, and she hit the child with that thing. On the legs, on the bum, on the upper body.”

Investigator: “How old was the kid?”

Maryna: “I think (name withheld) is now eight.”

During the course of our investigation we heard from many children: from those who’d left and from those still living at Jedidiah. This boy, we’ll call him ‘Michael’, seems to have been a regular target for physical abuse from Stephanie herself and her two adult sons, Stephan and Marco.

Investigator: “So all three of them hit you?”

‘Michael’: “Ja.”

Investigator: “What did they hit you with?”

‘Michael’: “Fist, pipes and stuff.”

Investigator: “Where did they hit you?”

‘Michael’: “On my face, on my back, on my ribs.”

This house meeting in September was recorded in secret on a cell phone. It’s hard to see what’s happening, but we can clearly hear Stephanie warning the children of what could happen should they dare leave her so-called sanctuary.

Stephanie: “(Name withheld) was put in an orphanage in Soshanguve… those k***irs raped him and beat him. Those bigger children can do… they stuck a 2 litre bottle in him.”

Charmaine: “She scares them, yes, so they’re very scared to talk to anybody that comes there.”

Stephanie: “I’m going to stick you in that place now. You’re next. You’re next. You too.”

Luke Lamprecht (JHB Child Advocacy Forum): “Well, my immediate reaction is that it’s monstrous.”

Luke Lamprecht is a one of the country’s most respected child and youth care practitioners.

Luke: “Because it’s this small group - and because the group is being threatened that, ‘I’m going to take you and drop you somewhere else, you can never leave here’ - you create this little pathological, perverse community in which anything goes and if anyone talks out there are these dire consequences to it.”

But this wasn’t all we discovered on the recording. What we heard next was hard to comprehend.

Stephanie: “Is this the first time you don’t have your underpants on?”

‘Michael’: “No, Mom.”

Stephanie: “Go get me a knife please.”

Stephanie is heard doling out punishment to ‘Michael’... His crime? Not wearing underpants.

Stephanie: “Go fetch me clothes pegs. I don’t give a f**k how you sleep, but you can’t play with your penis if you have underpants on.”

Charmaine: “So, she took a koki [pen]and she first wrote ‘tosser’... here you can see it, ‘tosser’ on his forehead, and she took two pegs and put it on his penis.”

‘Michael’: “Ouch!”

Stephanie: “Is that nice? Is that nice? It is nice, because you enjoy it. Is that nice? Oh, that’s nice (name withheld).”

‘Michael’: “I didn’t have underpants in my cupboard. They were all in the wash. And then she put ‘wasgoedpennetjies’ (clothes pegs).”

Stephanie: “Next time it’s a knife!”

Luke: “The sense I get of her is that she’s actually sadistic. It looks like - the things she does - there is an enjoyment in seeing children in pain.”

Many of the children placed here have been victims of sexual abuse. This girl told us how she’d ended up at Jedidiah after being raped by a family member. When Stephanie discovered the girl had been having sex with another teenage boy, she apparently lost it.

‘Susan’: “Soon after I arrived here, she already started saying that I’m a whore, that I molest children, which is not the truth.”

Derek: “And how did you feel when she was calling you a whore, a prostitute?”

‘Susan’: “I felt very humiliated, it hurt me a lot. She didn’t just say it to me, but in front of everyone.”

Derek: “How old were you then?”

‘Susan’: “Fourteen.”

Derek: ““Fourteen?”

‘Susan’: “Ja.”

Last year, a Constitutional Court ruling decriminalised consensual sex between adolescents 12 years and older. But the law is clear when it comes to under-16s having sex with adults. And Stephanie’s two sons, both over 18, stand accused of exactly that.

Charmaine: “I went to Stephan’s room and as I opened the door, Stephan was busy with (name withheld) on the bed, and I saw it.”

Derek: “They were having sex?”

Charmaine: “They were, yeah.”

It’s alleged that Stephanie was told on several occasions that her sons had been sleeping with underage girls in her care. She’s said to have lambasted the girls, not her
adult sons.

Maryna: “Then Aunty Steph started to say ugly things to (name withheld) - that she’s a little whore, and a bitch, and that she must go back to her parents because she slept
with Stephan.”

Luke: “As a person who’s in charge of a facility, if she was a person who was doing the correct thing, she would have gone and reported it and tried to get help and hold the offender accountable – who, in this case, happens to be her son.”

But Stephanie hasn’t reported her sons for statutory rape. Instead, in January, one of the minors in her care - a 15-year-old girl - married 25-year-old Marco, wearing Stephanie’s daughter’s wedding dress.

After the break, armed with our evidence, we confront Stephanie...

Stephanie: “I’ve got nothing to say, sorry...” [starts to walk away]

Derek: “Attaching a clothes peg to a little boy’s penis?”

We’ve been told that several sources have reported Stephanie to the authorities, but no action was ever taken. Concerned about what would happen to the 12 remaining children if we confronted her with our evidence, we asked for help from the top: Social Development Minister, Bathabile Dlamini. She seemed horrified by our footage and wanted the children immediately removed from Jedidiah.

Derek: “We met the minister at lunchtime. It’s 4:55pm and we are already on the way to the home with Mrs Dlamini, a welfare delegation, a police escort. And we were worried about where the children will be taken, but we have been assured that they will be in good hands.”

Derek: “Stephanie?”

Stephanie: “Yes.”

Derek: “We’ve had allegations of child abuse.”

Stephanie: “From whom?”

Derek: We’ve actually got video evidence.”

Stephanie: “I’m sorry...”

Derek: “Physically abusing and verbally abusing the children.”

Stephanie: “What can I say? I’ve got nothing to say, sorry.”

Derek: “Attaching a clothes peg to a little boy’s penis?”

Stephanie: “Who did it?”

Derek: “You did.”

Stephanie: “No! Never!”

Derek: “We have it on video.”

Stephanie: “Please, show me!”

Derek: “We’ll show you.”

Stephanie: “God, no!”

She told us there was only one child left with her. Several had been removed by social workers that very day.

Stephanie: “(Name withheld), he’s the only child in the Safe Haven. Social services came and fetched the kids this afternoon.”

Minister Dlamini: “This afternoon?”

Rob Bentley (Husband): “Well, we don’t want to keep them anymore, because we can’t afford them.”

Minister Dlamini: “Bring all of them then.”

Having initially told the Minister that there was only one boy left in her care, Stephanie then admitted there were others.

Stephanie: “Yes the one is (name withheld), and the other one is (name withheld).”

As Stephanie frantically flipped through her records, it became clear that Jedidiah had never been registered. The Minister demanded answers – how had social workers from her own department placed children in an unregistered home?

Minister Dlamini: “No, no, no. Don’t lie.”

As a frantic Stephanie looked on, the Minister questioned the social workers.

Social Worker: “Honourable minister. Our apologies.”

Minister Dlamini: “As a social worker I know that you don’t place children in a place that is not registered. We all know that! You’re not going to plead for people that are abusing children. You are a social worker.”

At this point Stephanie also turned on the social workers.

Stephanie: “Those children were left here for 22 weeks without any social worker ever coming to ever, ever visit them.”

Intent on defending herself, Stephanie bizarrely and unprofessionally disclosed this seven-year-old’s HIV status [on screen, identity obscured].

Stephanie: “No, definitely not. I mean, look at this beautiful young boy you just saw. He’s been here more than six months. He’s been here over a year; he’s HIV positive. Do you know of anyone that wants him?”

And then, without us having to show Stephanie the video, she started confessing.

Stephanie: “Do you know what; I’m going to be very honest with you... I’m a mother. Those are maybe two or three videos, but for seven years I’ve been doing this job and there was no complaint, no money from government, no help from government.”

When we arrived, Stephanie strongly denied putting a peg on ‘Michael’s’ penis.

[Earlier]
Stephanie: “Who did it?”
Derek: “You did.”
Stephanie: “No! Never!”
Derek: “We have it on video.”

But less than an hour later she explained why she’d done this.

Stephanie: “That child was weeing on the kids... not once, not twice. I begged him, I asked him very nicely, I asked him again, and I did put a peg on him.”

Derek: “What about calling a 14-year-old girl a whore?”

Stephanie: “If you only knew what she did... how many times.”

Derek: “But Stephanie you admit that you’ve been abusing the children?”

Stephanie: “Yes. Yes, and I can tell you that I don’t feel happy about that, but it’s very difficult to run a place where you don’t have help from anyone.”

But Stephanie didn’t only incriminate herself; she also admitted that her son Marco was guilty of statutory rape.

Stephanie: “Yes he did make her pregnant; yes they are married.”

Derek: “And she’s underage?”

Stephanie: “Yes, she’s 15.”

Eventually the Minister decided that the best option was to take the remaining two children to an actual place of safety.

Minister Dlamini: “We saw it today; it was not a good situation. I don’t want to start and explain what is in the video or film. Damage has been done.”

Whether Stephanie herself will be charged depends on a police investigation currently underway. Altogether 12 children have been removed and Jedidiah’s doors have been closed for good.

Stephanie: “Is this the first time you don’t have your underpants on?” ‘Michael’: “No, Mom.” Stephanie: “Go get me a knife please.” Stephanie is heard doling out punishment to ‘Michael’... His crime? Not wearing underpants. Stephanie: “Go fetch me clothes pegs. I don’t give a f**k how you sleep, but you can’t play with your penis if you have underpants on.” Charmaine: “So, she took a koki [pen]and she first wrote ‘tosser’... here you can see it, ‘tosser’ on his forehead, and she took two pegs and put it on his penis.” ‘Michael’: “Ouch!” Stephanie: “Is that nice? Is that nice? It is nice, because you enjoy it. Is that nice? Oh, that’s nice (name withheld).” ‘Michael’: “I didn’t have underpants in my cupboard. They were all in the wash. And then she put ‘wasgoedpennetjies’ (clothes pegs).” Stephanie: “Next time it’s a knife!” Luke: “The sense I get of her is that she’s actually sadistic. It looks like - the things she does - there is an enjoyment in seeing children in pain.” Many of the children placed here have been victims of sexual abuse. This girl told us how she’d ended up at Jedidiah after being raped by a family member. When Stephanie discovered the girl had been having sex with another teenage boy, she apparently lost it. ‘Susan’: “Soon after I arrived here, she already started saying that I’m a whore, that I molest children, which is not the truth.” Derek: “And how did you feel when she was calling you a whore, a prostitute?” ‘Susan’: “I felt very humiliated, it hurt me a lot. She didn’t just say it to me, but in front of everyone.” Derek: “How old were you then?” ‘Susan’: “Fourteen.” Derek: ““Fourteen?” ‘Susan’: “Ja.” Last year, a Constitutional Court ruling decriminalised consensual sex between adolescents 12 years and older. But the law is clear when it comes to under-16s having sex with adults. And Stephanie’s two sons, both over 18, stand accused of exactly that. Charmaine: “I went to Stephan’s room and as I opened the door, Stephan was busy with (name withheld) on the bed, and I saw it.” Derek: “They were having sex?” Charmaine: “They were, yeah.” It’s alleged that Stephanie was told on several occasions that her sons had been sleeping with underage girls in her care. She’s said to have lambasted the girls, not her adult sons. Maryna: “Then Aunty Steph started to say ugly things to (name withheld) - that she’s a little whore, and a bitch, and that she must go back to her parents because she slept with Stephan.” Luke: “As a person who’s in charge of a facility, if she was a person who was doing the correct thing, she would have gone and reported it and tried to get help and hold the offender accountable – who, in this case, happens to be her son.” But Stephanie hasn’t reported her sons for statutory rape. Instead, in January, one of the minors in her care - a 15-year-old girl - married 25-year-old Marco, wearing Stephanie’s daughter’s wedding dress. After the break, armed with our evidence, we confront Stephanie... Stephanie: “I’ve got nothing to say, sorry...” [starts to walk away] Derek: “Attaching a clothes peg to a little boy’s penis?” We’ve been told that several sources have reported Stephanie to the authorities, but no action was ever taken. Concerned about what would happen to the 12 remaining children if we confronted her with our evidence, we asked for help from the top: Social Development Minister, Bathabile Dlamini. She seemed horrified by our footage and wanted the children immediately removed from Jedidiah. Derek: “We met the minister at lunchtime. It’s 4:55pm and we are already on the way to the home with Mrs Dlamini, a welfare delegation, a police escort. And we were worried about where the children will be taken, but we have been assured that they will be in good hands.” Derek: “Stephanie?” Stephanie: “Yes.” Derek: “We’ve had allegations of child abuse.” Stephanie: “From whom?” Derek: We’ve actually got video evidence.” Stephanie: “I’m sorry...” Derek: “Physically abusing and verbally abusing the children.” Stephanie: “What can I say? I’ve got nothing to say, sorry.” Derek: “Attaching a clothes peg to a little boy’s penis?” Stephanie: “Who did it?” Derek: “You did.” Stephanie: “No! Never!” Derek: “We have it on video.” Stephanie: “Please, show me!” Derek: “We’ll show you.” Stephanie: “God, no!” She told us there was only one child left with her. Several had been removed by social workers that very day. Stephanie: “(Name withheld), he’s the only child in the Safe Haven. Social services came and fetched the kids this afternoon.” Minister Dlamini: “This afternoon?” Rob Bentley (Husband): “Well, we don’t want to keep them anymore, because we can’t afford them.” Minister Dlamini: “Bring all of them then.” Having initially told the Minister that there was only one boy left in her care, Stephanie then admitted there were others. Stephanie: “Yes the one is (name withheld), and the other one is (name withheld).” As Stephanie frantically flipped through her records, it became clear that Jedidiah had never been registered. The Minister demanded answers – how had social workers from her own department placed children in an unregistered home? Minister Dlamini: “No, no, no. Don’t lie.” As a frantic Stephanie looked on, the Minister questioned the social workers. Social Worker: “Honourable minister. Our apologies.” Minister Dlamini: “As a social worker I know that you don’t place children in a place that is not registered. We all know that! You’re not going to plead for people that are abusing children. You are a social worker.” At this point Stephanie also turned on the social workers. Stephanie: “Those children were left here for 22 weeks without any social worker ever coming to ever, ever visit them.” Intent on defending herself, Stephanie bizarrely and unprofessionally disclosed this seven-year-old’s HIV status [on screen, identity obscured]. Stephanie: “No, definitely not. I mean, look at this beautiful young boy you just saw. He’s been here more than six months. He’s been here over a year; he’s HIV positive. Do you know of anyone that wants him?” And then, without us having to show Stephanie the video, she started confessing. Stephanie: “Do you know what; I’m going to be very honest with you... I’m a mother. Those are maybe two or three videos, but for seven years I’ve been doing this job and there was no complaint, no money from government, no help from government.” When we arrived, Stephanie strongly denied putting a peg on ‘Michael’s’ penis. [Earlier] Stephanie: “Who did it?” Derek: “You did.” Stephanie: “No! Never!” Derek: “We have it on video.” But less than an hour later she explained why she’d done this. Stephanie: “That child was weeing on the kids... not once, not twice. I begged him, I asked him very nicely, I asked him again, and I did put a peg on him.” Derek: “What about calling a 14-year-old girl a whore?” Stephanie: “If you only knew what she did... how many times.” Derek: “But Stephanie you admit that you’ve been abusing the children?” Stephanie: “Yes. Yes, and I can tell you that I don’t feel happy about that, but it’s very difficult to run a place where you don’t have help from anyone.” But Stephanie didn’t only incriminate herself; she also admitted that her son Marco was guilty of statutory rape. Stephanie: “Yes he did make her pregnant; yes they are married.” Derek: “And she’s underage?” Stephanie: “Yes, she’s 15.” Eventually the Minister decided that the best option was to take the remaining two children to an actual place of safety. Minister Dlamini: “We saw it today; it was not a good situation. I don’t want to start and explain what is in the video or film. Damage has been done.” Whether Stephanie herself will be charged depends on a police investigation currently underway. Altogether 12 children have been removed and Jedidiah’s doors have been closed for good. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A place of safety that is anything but for young victims of abuse.
metadata.Summary: This is a story about Jedidiah Safe Haven in Haarties run by Stephanie Bentley. In 2012 three young children burned to death in a fire on the property. By all accounts this was a tragic accident, but since then another child has died, two have been removed by the court, volunteers have come forward with evidence and allegations of verbal and physical abuse, and the organization’s own auditor has raised red flags about their accounting practices. Belatedly, the Department of Social Development has decided to deregister the home and has instructed Christelike Maatskaplike Raad (CMR) to remove all of their children from Jedidiah. But almost two months later, ten children are still in Stephanie’s care. We ask, with clear evidence of abuse, why have the police not acted, and why were CMR children removed while the State’s wards have remained in this unhealthy environment?
metadata.Further information: Jedidiah Safe Haven has been in operation since 2008. It is a shelter run by Stephanie Bentley on the property owned by her husband, Rob. Safe Haven is supposed to provide temporary safe care for children who have been removed from their parents by the State. But it also makes private arrangements with parents to take on troubled teens, and when funds are running low homeless families or single mothers are invited to live on the property in exchange for cleaning and child care services. And although this is supposed to be a temporary home, many children have languished here for years. In 2012 three children died when the wendy-house they were sleeping in burnt down. By all accounts this was a tragic accident – the result of children playing with or having matches and candles in a wooden wendy-house. The deaths were widely publicized and reported on, but it appears that there was no proper investigation into the deaths and the question of whether Stephanie and her staff had been negligent. Should the deaths have raised red flags? Should it have triggered even a routine investigation by the police or the Department of Social Development? Had such an investigation been done they may have found evidence of the following: • Mental and verbal abuse • Physical abuse • Statutory rape Last year a police reservist approached Carte Blanche with allegations of these issues. He in turn put us in touch with a former volunteer as well as a former resident who also claimed to know about abuse at the home. The former resident – Charmaine – handed over audio and video recordings of going-on at Safe Haven. She claims to have recorded these on her cellphone in the weeks prior to her being evicted from the home. The recordings suggest the children are mentally and verbally abused by Stephanie. There are also suggestions of physical and sexual abuse, but these are not explicit. This evidence was handed over to the Department of Social Development last year who instructed CMR to remove their kids from Safe Haven. But three months later the State's own wards have remained in this unhealthy environment, including a 15-year-old girl who according to sources is pregnant with Stephanie's son's child and recently married him despite being under the age of consent. We have also spoken to Safe Haven's former auditor who has confirmed that there are many questionable practices with their finances which led him to issue them with a qualified audit. We intend to approach the Department of Social Development to ask them to work with us to remove the remaining children from Safe Haven. Although the Department is unlikely to come off looking good, the blame appears to lie with the provincial Department, and action by the Minister may put her in a good light. We intend to conduct interviews with the various sources before the Department removes the kids so that we will be ready to confront Stephanie and run the story as soon as the kids are removed.
metadata.Reason for hidden camera: We have been provided with hidden camera footage from a source - this shows evidence of abuse. We have also filmed our own hidden camera footage - this was so that we could obtain footage of Stephanie Bentley.
metadata.Reason for legal: This story involves serious allegations of abuse again minor children. There is the potential that by identifying the home that we will identify the children. We have already met with Okyerebea about this story.
